reason: E2 shows annealing-induced SRO clusters in a similar HEA, supporting the first premise. However, no cited evidence links SRO to modified electron-phonon coupling or enhanced superconductivity, leaving the core mechanistic premises unsupported. The alloy's single-phase stability and specific annealing conditions are also not directly evidenced.
premises: Thermal annealing of HEAs can induce short-range chemical ordering (SRO) clusters
SRO clusters locally modify electron-phonon coupling
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling increases Tc and sharpens the transition in BCS superconductors
The proposed Ti–Zr–Hf–V–Mo alloy can form a single-phase solid solution amenable to SRO
Annealing at ~600°C will induce SRO without phase separation or long-range order
